messages.subject: Lack of robustness
parts: I don't like to look a gift horse in the mouth, but the last few days have left me feeling very frustrated with Stan. To begin with, I spent over a day -- on a project that is already nearly two weeks over-due -- fighting with a problem that turned out to be caused by issues with Stan's implementation of the CDF for the negative binomial function. So I had to redo my model to avoid use of negative binomial. No sooner had I done that, then I ran into another problem: Stan doesn't handle zero-length vectors correctly. In attempting to work around that problem I ran into yet another bug: using max() in declaring the dimensions of a vector/matrix causes Stan to generate C++ code that fails to compile. I am worn out from fighting with this software right now.

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Lack of robustness
parts:
Hi Kevin,

Sorry to hear about your frustration. I wish we knew about it earlier: I'm sure one of the devs would have been more than happy to help you out before this point. 

The development team is trying hard to balance the want to implement new features and making the existing ones more robust. We prioritize bugs, so we'll address the issues you've created as soon as we can hunt down the cause and fix it properly.

Sorry about the zero-length vectors not working. At some point I had made sure all of the Stan language could handle it properly, but the language has grown a lot and this was also before optimization was available in Stan. I'll try to verify, fix, and prevent this from breaking in the future sometime soon.

Regarding numeric stability: repeatable examples are immensely helpful. Thanks for working through that. Michael had also run into the problem independently. We're concerned with the numeric stability of all our functions, but we don't have enough resources to test every possible value for every function, so when users run into trouble, it's really helpful to know what fails. Sorry you ran into it before we patched it; thanks for identifying the problem.

Stan language parsing, but failing to compile: that's our bad. We'll fix that asap. That should never happen. 

Hopefully the next time you're back to using Stan, it'll be more robust to your problems. If you get frustrated, feel free to email sooner rather than later.



Daniel
